text:
The value of the definite integral

$\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{4}}^{\frac{π}{4}}\frac{dx}{(1+e^{x\cos x})(\sin ^{4}x+\cos ^{4}x)}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{4}}^{\frac{π}{4}}\frac{dx}{(1+e^{x\cos x})(\sin ^{4}x+\cos ^{4}x)}$ .... (1)

Using $\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x)dx=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(a+b-x)dx$

$I=\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{4}}^{\frac{π}{4}}\frac{dx}{(1+e^{-x\cos x})(\sin ^{4}x+\cos ^{4}x)}$

Add (1) and (2)

$2I=\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{4}}^{\frac{π}{4}}\frac{dx}{\sin ^{4}x+\cos ^{4}x}$

$2I=2\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}\frac{dx}{\sin ^{4}x+\cos ^{4}x}$

$I=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}\frac{\left (1+\frac{1}{\tan 2x}\right )\sec ^{2}x}{\left (\tan -\frac{1}{\tan x}\right )^{2}+2}dx$

$\tan x-\frac{1}{\tan x}=t$

$\left (1+\frac{1}{\tan ^{2}x}\right )\sec ^{2}xdx=dt$

$I=\int\limits _{-\infty }^{0}\frac{dt}{t^{2}+2}=\left [\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{t}{\sqrt{2}}\right )\right ]_{-\infty }^{0}$

$I=0-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left (-\frac{π}{2}\right )=\frac{π}{2\sqrt{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: A ray of light through (2, 1) is reflected at a point P on the y-axis and then passes through the point (5, 3). If this reflected ray is the directrix of an ellipse with eccentricity $\frac{1}{3}$ and the distance of the nearer focus from this directrix is $\frac{8}{\sqrt{53}}$, then the equation of the other directrix can be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By the law of reflection at the $y$-axis, the reflected ray passes through the image of $(2,1)$ in the $y$-axis, namely $(-2,1)$, and also through $(5,3)$.


[IMG]

Its equation is

$y-1=\dfrac{3-1}{5-(-2)}(x+2)\Rightarrow 2x-7y+11=0$

For an ellipse with semi-major axis $a$ and eccentricity $e$, the nearer focus is at distance $\dfrac{a}{e}-ae$ from a directrix. With $e=\dfrac{1}{3}$:

$3a-\dfrac{a}{3}=\dfrac{8a}{3}=\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{53}}\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{53}}$

The two directrices are parallel and $\dfrac{2a}{e}=6a=\dfrac{18}{\sqrt{53}}$ apart. Taking the other directrix as $2x-7y+λ=0$:

$\dfrac{|λ-11|}{\sqrt{53}}=\dfrac{18}{\sqrt{53}}\Rightarrow λ=29\text{or}λ=-7$

So the other directrix is $2x-7y+29=0$ or $2x-7y-7=0$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: If the coefficients of $x^{7}$ in $\left (x^{2}+\frac{1}{bx}\right )^{11}$ and $x^{-7}$ in $\left (x-\frac{1}{bx^{2}}\right )^{11}$, b $\neq$ 0, are equal, then the value of b is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Coefficient of $x^{7}$ in $\left (x^{2}+\frac{1}{bx}\right )^{11}$ :

General Term = ${}^{11}C_{r}(x^{2})^{11-r}.\left (\frac{1}{bx}\right )^{r}$

= ${}^{11}C_{r}x^{22-3r}.\frac{1}{b^{r}}$

$22-3r=7$

$r=5$

$\therefore$ Required Term = ${}^{11}C_{5}.\frac{1}{b^{5}}.x^{7}$

Coefficient of $x^{-7}$ in $\left (x-\frac{1}{bx^{2}}\right )^{11}$ :

General Term = ${}^{11}C_{r}(x)^{11-r}.\left (-\frac{1}{bx^{2}}\right )^{r}$

= ${}^{11}C_{r}x^{11-3r}.\frac{(-1)^{r}}{b^{r}}$

$11-3r=-7$ $\therefore$ $r=6$

$\therefore$ Required Term = ${}^{11}C_{6}.\frac{1}{b^{6}}x^{-7}$

According to the question,

${}^{11}C_{5}.\frac{1}{b^{5}}={}^{11}C_{6}.\frac{1}{b^{6}}$

Since, b $\neq$ 0 $\therefore$ b = 1
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 4 \end{array}\right ]$. If $A^{-1} =$ $α$I + $β$A, $α$, $β$ $\in$ R, I is a 2 $\times$ 2 identity matrix then 4($α$ $-$ $β$) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 4 \end{array}\right ],|A|=6$

$A^{-1}=\frac{adjA}{|A|}=\frac{1}{6}\left [\begin{array}{ll} 4 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{1}{6} & \frac{1}{6} \end{array}\right ]$

$\left [\begin{array}{ll} \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{1}{6} & \frac{1}{6} \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} α & 0 \\ 0 & α \end{array}\right ]+\left [\begin{array}{ll} β & 2β \\ -β & 4β \end{array}\right ]$

$\left. \begin{array}{l} α+β=\frac{2}{3} \\ β=-\frac{1}{6} \end{array}\right \}\Rightarrow α=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{6}=\frac{5}{6}$

$\therefore$ $4(α-β)=4(1)=4$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: Let f : R $\to$ R be a function such that f(2) = 4 and f'(2) = 1. Then, the value of $\lim _{x\to 2}\frac{x^{2}f(2)-4f(x)}{x-2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $f(2)=4$, the numerator is $4x^{2}-4f(x)$, which vanishes at $x=2$. Splitting it with $f(2)=4$:

$\frac{x^{2}f(2)-4f(x)}{x-2}=\frac{4(x^{2}-4)-4(f(x)-f(2))}{x-2}=4(x+2)-4\cdot \frac{f(x)-f(2)}{x-2}$

As $x\to 2$, $4(x+2)\to 16$ and $\dfrac{f(x)-f(2)}{x-2}\to f^{'}(2)=1$, so

$\lim _{x\to 2}\frac{x^{2}f(2)-4f(x)}{x-2}=16-4(1)=12$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text:
For real numbers $α$ and $β$, consider the following system of linear equations :

x + y $-$ z = 2, x + 2y + $α$z = 1, 2x $-$ y + z = $β$. If the system has infinite solutions, then $α$ + $β$ is equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For infinite solutions

$\Delta$ = $\Delta_{1}$ = $\Delta_{2}$ = $\Delta_{3}$ = 0

$\Delta$ = $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & α \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & α \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Delta$ = 3(2 + $α$) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = $-$2

$\Delta _{2}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 2 & β & 1 \end{array}\right |=0$

1(1 + 2$β$) $-$2(1 + 4) $-$ ($β$ $-$ 2) = 0

 $β$ $-$ 7 = 0

$β$ = 7

$\therefore$ $α$ + $β$ = 5

text: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k},\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}=\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$ be three vectors such that $\vec{a}\times \vec{b}=\vec{c}$ and $\vec{a}\quad .\vec{b}=1$. sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{a}\times \vec{b}=\vec{c}$

Take Dot with $\vec{c}$

$\left (\vec{a}\times \vec{b}\right ).\vec{c}=\left |\vec{c}\right |^{2}=2$

Projection of $\vec{b}$ on $\vec{a}\times \vec{c}=l$

$\frac{\left |\vec{b}.(\vec{a}\times \vec{c})\right |}{|\vec{a}\times \vec{c}|}=l$

$\therefore$ $l=\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}\Rightarrow l^{2}=\frac{4}{6}$

$3l^{2}=2$

Let the domain of the function

$f(x)=\log _{4}\left (\log _{5}\left (\log _{3}(18x-x^{2}-77)\right )\right )$ be (a, b). Then the value of the integral $\int\limits _{a}^{b}\frac{\sin ^{3}x}{\sin ^{3}x+\sin ^{3}(a+b-x)}dx$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For domain

$\log _{5}\left (\log _{3}(18x-x^{2}-77)\right )>0$

$\log _{3}(18x-x^{2}-77)>1$

$18x-x^{2}-77>3$

$x^{2}-18x+80<0$

$x\in (8,10)$

$\Rightarrow$ a = 8 and b = 10

$I=\int\limits _{a}^{b}\frac{\sin ^{3}x}{\sin ^{3}x+\sin ^{3}(a+b-x)}dx$

$I=\int\limits _{a}^{b}\frac{\sin ^{3}(a+b-x)}{\sin ^{3}x+\sin ^{3}(a+b-x)}$

$2I=(b-a)\Rightarrow I=\frac{b-a}{2}$ ($\because$ a = 8 and b = 10)

$I=\frac{10-8}{2}=1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift
